title: Safe experimentation playbook for automated batching + KV-cache recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an A/B experimentation framework and runbooks for applying automated batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations with safe canarying and deterministic rollback. The goal is to deliver measurable per-token cost reductions while preserving latency SLOs and error rate thresholds. This ticket covers experiment design, telemetry/metric definitions, dashboard panels, statistical analysis approach, rollout automation hooks, and failure/rollback runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Defined primary and secondary metrics and thresholds (cost delta, p95 latency, error rate, cache hit ratio, model output quality proxies).
Implementation of experiment assignment mechanism (deterministic hashing by customer_id -> variant).
Dashboards in Grafana with per-variant panels and automated anomaly alerts.
Automated canary apply/rollback playbooks wired to rollout service so a failed canary triggers immediate rollback.

A complete testrun with at least 14 days of production-weighted traffic or equivalent synthetic load demonstrating statistically significant cost savings without latency regressions for one model family.
metrics: primary: net_cost_per_1k_tokens (USD) — end-to-end inference cost including infra and token accounting
primary: p95_token_latency_ms (ms) — 95th percentile token generation latency
secondary: error_rate_percent — request-level error rate (5xx/timeout/failed decode)
secondary: cache_hit_ratio_percent — KV cache hit rate for prefix reuse
secondary: effective_batch_size_distribution — histogram of batch sizes over 1h windows
secondary: avg_tokens_per_request — changes in request token distribution
quality_proxy: rerank_consistency / hallucination_signal_count — coarse signal from eval prompts
operational: rollback_time_seconds — time from alert to completed rollback
safety: user_impacted_requests_percent — percent of requests experiencing degraded output quality alerts
experiment_design: Variant assignment: deterministic modulo hash(customer_id) -> control/variant to ensure consistent user experience across requests.
Population: 5% of global traffic as initial canary; scale to 25% if metrics within thresholds for 48h; full rollout gated by statistical tests.
Stat test: bootstrap of cost metric + Welch's t-test for latency with alpha=0.01 and pre-specified minimum detectable effect (MDE) = 2% cost reduction or 5ms p95 latency increase.
Duration: run until sample size requirements met OR 14 days of steady traffic; use sequential testing early stopping with alpha-spending to control false positives.
Stratification: ensure variants are balanced across model family, region, and customer tier to avoid confounded effects.
Quality checks: include a small set (~200) of deterministic eval prompts run in both variants to detect output divergence; flag large semantic deltas for human review.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): run offline simulation with trace-replay for 72h using historical traces and cached KV warm-start to estimate hit ratio and batching changes.
Phase 1 (canary-1): 5% traffic, 6h warm-up, monitor metrics every 5m; auto-hold if p95 latency increases > 7.5ms or error_rate +0.2% absolute.
Phase 2 (canary-2): 25% traffic for 48h if Phase 1 passes; additional checks on rerank_consistency and cache_hit_ratio trend.
Phase 3 (ramp): linear ramp to target population (50-100%) with incremental checks and manual approval step at 50%.

Automated rollback: Alert rule triggers rollout-service automation which reverses config and flags PR with a postmortem template. Rollback must complete within defined window (<5min for hosted API routes).
Safe-config apply: apply atomic per-route config with feature-flag gating and warmup TTL for KV caches to avoid cold-start thundering herd.

decisions: Use deterministic hashing by customer_id for variant sticky assignment to preserve session consistency.
Adopt sequential testing with pre-specified alpha spending to allow early stopping while reducing false positives.
Quality proxy (rerank_consistency) will gate any rollout beyond 25% if divergence > 0.7 on the eval set.
Rollback automation will be implemented in rollout-service and must include an automated PR and an incident channel notification.
